segments: and dragged her {him?}:
and threw him down from his throne upon his face.
And all of them gathered against him,
and they dragged him out on foot from the palace,
and took him away and imprisoned him in the residence of Mu'izz al-Dawla, the commander of the army.
And they brought al-Fadl son of al-Muqtadir and made him king,
and named him al-Muti'.
after he had been deposed, he lived twenty-nine years and five months.
When the magnates seated this man on the throne,
they brought al-Mustakfi before him, and he submitted to him,
and testified against himself regarding his abdication;
and he was imprisoned in the palace.
And in that same year in which al-Muti' began to reign,
which was the year
334 of the Arabs,
two magnates waged war against each other:
one was Nasir al-Dawla ibn Hamdan, ruler of Mosul,
and the other was Mu'izz al-Dawla, who had set up al-Muti'.
And Nasir came and seized the eastern side of Baghdad,
and Mu'izz the western side.
Then Mu'izz grew bold and crossed over to the eastern side,
and Nasir fled in the direction of Mosul.
And the people of the city also on that side, when they feared the sword of Mu'izz,
went out headlong to flee toward Mosul,
men and women.
And many died on the way from thirst and exhaustion,
especially women who were not accustomed to walking.
A certain woman from among the daughters of the nobles was seen lying beside the road in noble garments,
with a purse in her hand,
and wailing:
"Behold, four hundred dinars!
Take them and give me a little water to drink!"
And no one paid attention to her,
nor did anyone even take the purse from her hand for free,
but everyone was engrossed with their own life in flight.
For ten thousand souls {OCR?} perished in this flight.
And when Mu'izz heard these things, he proclaimed peace,
and brought out water for the fugitives and brought them back.
And it is said
that in their lives the Babylonians had never seen distress like that of that day.
It is said
that there was a certain demoniac man at that time in Baghdad,
and he used to speak of future events in a state of trance {OCR?}.
This man, days before, had been crying out in the markets and saying:
"Teach your women,
O sons of Baghdad,
barefootedness,
and accustom them to be afflicted,
because the distress is near!"
And so it happened.
And in that same year there was a great famine in Baghdad,
